newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL COFFEE TO SEE COOLER TEMPS, NO FROST - SOMAR.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL COFFEE TO SEE COOLER TEMPS, NO FROST - SOMAR.

text.p: Temperatures in key Brazilian coffee regions should fall over the coming weekend due to the passage of a polar air mass but no frosts are forecast, local meteorologists Somar said on Thursday in a weather update.
The region north of Parana should see minimum temperatures of seven degrees Celsius on the night of August 9/early morning of August 10 as the polar air mass moves out to sea.

The tail end of the air mass should lead to cooler weather in more northern regions on the nights of August 10-11, with lowest temperatures forecast at five to seven degrees Celsius in highland areas of south Minas Gerais and no frosts forecast.
Long-term models point to another air mass which is expected to have an intensity of 1,030 millibars in the southern Pacific on August 12.
This system should reach the coffee regions on August 15-16 and should lead to another cool period.
"In my opinion, this one could be more dangerous as there should be no cloud cover," said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
"If the air mass comes in in the south of the country, there should be no problem. But if it comes in further to the north, there could be some risk to coffee," he added.
This was still a long-term forecast however and was very much subject to change, Massari said.
June and July are normally the most dangerous months for frost but the past month has been unusually warm which meteorologists have attributed to the development of the El Nino weather phenomenon.
It looks however as if this current month will be colder than July although that does not necessarily mean that it will be colder than normal, Massari said.
